Setup (per docs/research/variance_of_associator.md § "Worked example:
single Fano generator"):
A(a, b, c) := ‖[a, b, c]‖²   where [a,b,c] = (a·b)·c − a·(b·c)
Unperturbed: [a,b,c] = 2·e_7, A = 4.

variance (from the β document, derivation):
Var(A) ≈ 64 σ²                                (TRUTH)
If the current compiler's stepwise scalar-product rule were applied
instead, it would give:
Var_compiler(A) ≈ 16 σ²                       (COMPILER, 4× low)
This test computes the sample variance of A over N = 100,000 Monte
Carlo samples and compares to the TRUTH formula. It does NOT test the
compiler's variance_of() — that requires the full Knowledge<f64>
chain which introduces unrelated complexities (see ζ buffer bug). The
compiler comparison is deferred to a separate test.
Pass criterion: |MC_var − 64σ²| / 64σ² < 0.05 (5% relative error).
If this passes, β's analytical formula is validated empirically. The
remaining claim — that the compiler produces 16σ² — is then a
separate reading-confirmation task.

within-organ redistribution is instantaneous but Q-transport between
blood and tissue remains rate-limited. The hierarchy is
PBPK28-literature → PBPK14 → 1-state QSS
with monotonically decreasing model-form complexity. Discrepancies

1. Build adjacency matrix (synthetic connectome, 8 nodes)
2. Compute graph Laplacian
3. Extract 7 eigenvectors via deflated power iteration
4. Map eigenvectors to octonion basis (ψ_k ↔ e_k)
5. Compute G₂ 3-form on the eigenvector frame
6. Compute SU(3) branching quality
7. Run null model (random SO(7) rotations)
8. Compare observed vs null → p-value estimate

T3: Null distribution has lower mean |φ| than observed

T5: Associator deviation field computable on extracted frame

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `knowledge_layout_shadows_user_field_name`. A user struct field named `value` was silently clobbered by its sibling. `ir_register_knowledge_layout` preseeds a synthetic `Knowledge` layout — value@0, variance@1, confidence@2 — as entry 0 of the struct layout table,. description: A user struct field named `value` was silently clobbered by its sibling. `ir_register_knowledge_layout` preseeds a synthetic `Knowledge` layout — value@0, variance@1, confidence@2 — as entry 0 of the struct layout table,
comments: A user struct field named `value` was silently clobbered by its sibling.
`ir_register_knowledge_layout` preseeds a synthetic `Knowledge` layout —
value@0, variance@1, confidence@2 — as entry 0 of the struct layout table,
before any user struct is registered. `field_idx_from_name_simple` resolves a
field *name* to a slot by scanning the whole table in order and taking the
first hit in any struct, and that path is what runs whenever the base is not
a typed local: `arr[i].f` reaches it because array locals record a length but
no element type.
So `ext[0].value` resolved to Knowledge's slot 0 — the same slot as `oid` —
and `ext[0].value = val_buf` overwrote the `oid` written just before it. Both
reads then went to slot 0 too, so `value` read back correct while `oid`
returned `value`'s bytes: a silent wrong answer at rc=0, with no diagnostic.
The trigger was the identifier, not the shape. The same program with the
field named `val` was always correct, at any struct size, array length or
index form — which is why size- and index-threshold hypotheses all died.
Guard all three preseeded names. Anything reading its sibling's data here
means the synthetic layout is shadowing user layouts again.
Honest scope: CI runs this suite under souc-stage2, which never carried the
defect, so this file is green either way there — it is the readable witness,
not the guard. The discriminating gate is the `knowledge_field_shadow` case
in tests/madaros/source_to_elf/manifest.tsv, which compiles with Madaros and
was measured red before this fix and green after.

description: hessian_of over the quotient rule. Before this rule existed the division branch cleared the Hessian outright. That was the honest choice at the time -- a missing number rather than an
comments: hessian_of over the quotient rule.
Before this rule existed the division branch cleared the Hessian outright.
That was the honest choice at the time -- a missing number rather than an
operand's Hessian wearing the quotient's name -- but it meant every ratio
in the clinical corpus (clearance over volume, dose over weight, any
concentration) had a second-order term of exactly zero, and no diagnostic
said so. A confident zero from a shipped builtin is indistinguishable
from a true zero at the call site.
H(a/b)_jk = a_jk/b - (a_j*b_k + a_k*b_j)/b^2 - a*b_jk/b^2 + 2*a*b_j*b_k/b^3
h_bb is the row that pins the rule. A two-term approximation -- the part
that looks like the product rule with a reciprocal -- reproduces h_ab
exactly and gets h_bb wrong, so the mixed partial alone cannot tell a
correct implementation from a plausible one.

back as 0.000000 under -O -- the shadow value is an f64 reached through this
same marker -- and why tests/run-pass/knowledge_octonion_structure.sio lost

Returning a nested array literal from a function declared to return a 2-D
array is rejected: `error: return type does not match function signature`.
The flat case is accepted, so the gap is specific to the nested encoding. The
declared type comes from scan_type and the literal builds its own hash from
its first element, and the two do not agree. Element size is NOT the
discriminator -- [[f64; 1]; 2], whose inner element is 8 bytes, is rejected
too, so a first guess that scan_type computes a real element size while the
literal hardcodes 8 is disproven.
This matters beyond arrays. The return-type check currently reports through
tc_error, which prints "warning: " and does not fail the build (see the note
at its definition). Pointing it at tc_error_hard makes it fatal and works --
it correctly rejects hello.sio and bdf_stiff.sio, which really are ill-typed
-- but it also rejects this, and stdlib/numerical/linalg.sio mat7_to_nested,
which are correct. So the return position cannot be made to fail a build
until this is fixed, and that is the whole dependency: nothing else in the
study's 24 modules or in 1893 run-pass tests is affected.
When this passes, drop the ignore, and the return check can become fatal.

comments: FRENTE B, vector 4/3 — the basis-aligned octonion census in the sedenion (a verified fingerprint).
A basis-aligned octonion candidate is a 3-dim F₂ subspace of the sedenion index space F₂⁴ (its 7
nonzero vectors, XOR-closed); there are 15. This test certifies three exact partitions of them:
* NSUB = 15 subspaces total;
* ZDFREE = 8 are zero-divisor-free (genuine octonion / division algebra); the other 7 contain a
zero divisor — the quasi-octonions (matches Cawagas, Discuss. Math. 2004: 7 quasi-octonions carry
the sedenion zero divisors);
* PURE = 1 is "Clifford-pure" — has ALL C(7,2)=21 internal ambient left-mult pairs anticommuting
({L_i,L_j}=0 in the 16-dim Cℓ(8), see sedenion_clifford8.md): the base octonion {e_1..e_7}.
* Through the base quaternion ⟨e_1,e_2,e_3⟩={1,2,3}, the three copies (3rd generator c∈{4,8,12}) have
ambient-L non-anticommuting-pair counts {0, 6, 12}.
These three properties are DISTINCT (8 ZD-free ⊋ 1 Clifford-pure); do not conflate them.
INTERPRETATION (honest boundary). This fingerprint is CONSISTENT WITH — it illustrates, it does not
prove — Erratum E1's claim that Gresnigt's three family-S₃ octonion copies are non-monomial: only the
base octonion is Clifford-pure, so the ambient embedding already distinguishes it. The non-monomiality
of the FAMILY S₃ rests on Brown's theorem (Aut(𝕊)=G₂×S₃), not on this census; and PSL(2,7) itself
contains S₃ subgroups, so a basis-index census cannot by itself separate the family-S₃ from an S₃
inside the monomial-168. Reported as an executed algebraic fingerprint, not a group-theoretic proof.
Uses e_i·e_j = σ(i,j)·e_{i⊕j}; {L_i,L_j}=0 via σ(i,j⊕c)σ(j,c)+σ(j,i⊕c)σ(i,c)=0 ∀c; a zero-divisor
pair (e_a±e_b)(e_c±e_d)=0 via componentwise integer zero. Decidable integer arithmetic, no float.
SELF-CONTAINED. Cross-verified vs the oracle by the gate + Lean.

A tuple-returning function that CALLS another tuple-returning function used to destroy its caller's aggregate-return pointer. description: A tuple-returning function that CALLS another tuple-returning function used to destroy its caller's aggregate-return pointer. The x86 SRET prologue is `push rbp; mov rbp,rsp; push r12; sub rsp,frame`, so
comments: A tuple-returning function that CALLS another tuple-returning function used to
destroy its caller's aggregate-return pointer.
The x86 SRET prologue is `push rbp; mov rbp,rsp; push r12; sub rsp,frame`, so
the saved r12 lives at rbp-0x08 -- which was also slot 1, where the incoming
SRET pointer was stored. `pop r12` then restored that pointer instead of the
caller's r12, and the caller wrote its result through a pointer into the
callee's dead frame. The next call reused those bytes, so every binding read
the LAST call's values.
Confirmed under gdb: r12 intact at the callee's entry, holding the callee's
own SRET at its `ret`. Fixed by reserving slot 1 for the pushed r12.
Two bindings minimum: with one, a stale pointer still reads its own values.

source; the rule cannot PROVE the sources disjoint, so it fails closed and
refuses. Unknown is never treated as disjoint -- assuming independence one
cannot certify is exactly the anti-garbling this rule exists to prevent.

is refused, so this compile-fail fixture supersedes it as the top-operand

rule and not an unrelated error.

comments: This was tests/known-gaps/units/derived_unit_dropped_by_inference.sio, a
reproduction of a gap that is now CLOSED (2026-09-05). It used to PASS: a
quotient lost its dimension, so mol/cm3 + K compiled. It is here, and not
there, because a file that must be refused belongs with the other refusals.
What closed it: the dimension is carried through `*` and `/` (dim_add /
dim_sub at the multiplicative site) and the additive check compares it. Both
backends carry it, so this is refused under --target aarch64-linux too --
which is what scripts/ci/a64_compile_fail_parity_gate.sh now asserts for this
file along with the rest of the corpus.
